# posthog-flags-to-notion

Sync PostHog feature flags to a Notion database. Resolves opaque group IDs to real customer names so your whole team can see which flags are on and for whom.

## Usage

Three entry points:

1. **Claude Code agent** — `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emichy/posthog-flags-to-notion/main/install.sh | bash` drops the agent at `~/.claude/agents/feature-flags.md`. Uses the Notion MCP server. No npm install required.
2. **MCP server** — `npx posthog-flags-to-notion --mcp` exposes tools (`list_flags`, `sync_flags_to_notion`, `lookup_group`, `flags_for_group`) for Cursor and other MCP clients.
3. **CLI** — `npx posthog-flags-to-notion` runs a one-shot sync. `--dry-run` previews without writing.

## How it works

1. Fetches all feature flags from the PostHog API
2. Parses targeting rules — flags targeting specific groups get their IDs extracted; percentage rollouts get a plain-English summary
3. Resolves group IDs to names using PostHog's Groups API (with exact `group_key` match to avoid false positives from fuzzy search)
4. Builds a reverse index of `groupId → [flagKeys]` so the directory table can show which flags each group is in
5. Writes results to Notion — creates new rows, updates existing ones, archives flags that no longer exist in PostHog
6. Never writes to the `Notes` column — reserved for manual annotations

## Configuration

Required env vars (CLI + MCP server only — the Claude Code agent prompts for these conversationally):
- `POSTHOG_API_KEY` — PostHog personal API key
- `POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID` — your PostHog project ID
- `NOTION_API_KEY` — Notion integration token
- `NOTION_DATABASE_ID` — Notion database for the flag table

Optional:
- `POSTHOG_HOST` — defaults to `https://us.posthog.com`, use `https://eu.posthog.com` for EU
- `POSTHOG_GROUP_TYPE_INDEX` — which group type to resolve (default: `0`)
- `POSTHOG_GROUP_PROPERTY_KEY` — the property key in flag filters (default: `project_id`)
- `NOTION_DIRECTORY_DATABASE_ID` — optional second database for group lookup
- `SKIP_SURVEY_FLAGS` — skip `survey-targeting-*` flags **only when they have no project targeting** (default: `true`)

## Notion schema (auto-created)

Flag table:
- title column (whatever you named it) — flag name from PostHog
- `Flag Key` (rich_text) — short flag key, e.g. `new_ui`. Dedup uses this column.
- `Status` (select) — Active / Inactive / Archived
- `Targeting` (rich_text) — summary of targeting rules
- `Groups Enabled` (rich_text) — comma-separated resolved group names
- `PostHog URL` (url) — link to the flag in PostHog
- `Last Synced` (date) — date of last sync
- `Notes` (rich_text) — **never written by the tool**; safe for manual annotations

Directory table (optional):
- title column — group name
- `Group ID` (rich_text) — PostHog group key, deduplicated
- `Tier` (rich_text) — from `active_tier` group property
- `Feature Flags` (multi_select) — every flag key that targets this group

## Resilience

- Notion API calls are rate-limited (~3 req/s) with 429 retry
- Group lookups require an exact `group_key` match before trusting a row
- `Flag Key` matching is type-agnostic — works whether the column is rich_text, url, or title-typed
- Re-runs are idempotent: one row per flag, one row per group, regardless of how many flags reference a group
- Refuses to sync if PostHog returns zero flags (prevents wiping the Notion table on a misconfigured API key)
